newsitem.title: USA: NYS revenue total collections now $1.36 bln-state.
newsitem.headline: NYS revenue total collections now $1.36 bln-state.

text.p: Continued economic growth in New York State has generated additional state revenue collections totaling $500 million, which brings total revenue to $1.36 billion, state budget director Patricia Woodworth said Thursday.

Based on the most recent tax collection data available, the Division of the Budget now believes the state will have approximately $500 million more in revenue, which brings total available revenue to $1.36 billion.

Of the $1.4 billion surplus from the fiscal year 1997 budget, which ended March 31, $1.05 billion has been previously identified and included as part of Gov. George Pataki's proposed fiscal 1998 executive budget. That leaves $370 million in additional unbudgeted surplus revenues, the budget office said in a release.

In addition, for fiscal year 1998, which began April 1, there is another $490 million that resulted from the consensus revenue forecasting conference, which brought total available revenue to $860 million prior to Thursday's announcement, the budget office said.

The Division of Budget of said it indicates that 1996 will generate nearly $500 million more in revenue than it had expected at the time of the consensus revenue forecasting conference held in mid-March and higher than the highest of the revenue estimates presented at the conference.
